newsitem.title: BELGIUM: DANISH BASTIONEN BUYS BRUSSELS EU BUILDING.
newsitem.headline: DANISH BASTIONEN BUYS BRUSSELS EU BUILDING.

text.p: The Belgian state sold a Brussels building rented to the European Parliament to Danish real estate group Bastionen A/S for 1.37 billion Belgian francs at a public auction on Tuesday.

The nine-floor Van Maerlant building -- well-known in Brussels because of its landmark bridge over Rue Belliard -- is rented to the EU until March 2007 for 144 million francs per year. It has a useable office space of 28,133 square meters.
"This is an important investment for us because it is an EU building, because of its situation at the heart of the European district," Bastionen executive John Frederiksen told Reuters.
The Van Maerlant complex houses offices for members of the parliament, meeting rooms, a restaurant and two bars.
The bridge across Rue Belliard -- which connects the building to European Parliament offices owned by private Belgian real estate fund Cofinimmo-- is included in the transaction.
At auction the state sold two other properties to reduce state debt.
Frederiksen said Bastionen, one of Denmark's largest real estate groups, was looking for further acquisitions in Brussels.
Last year the group bought a building at Boulevard du Triomphe for 700 million francs.
Frederiksen said his group had a real estate portfolio worth about 220 million pound sterling, of which 30 percent in Denmark and the rest abroad, mainly in the UK, the Netherlands and Belgium.
